title: Write a parametrized suite that catches six seeded bugs
problem: duration.py has a correct parse_duration() ('1h30m' -> 5400). This time you write the tests. Grow the VALID and INVALID tables in test_duration.py from the spec in the docstring, and write test_invalid with pytest.raises(match=). test_meta.py runs your tables against six buggy versions of parse_duration: every bug must make at least one of your rows fail.
requirements: Edit only test_duration.py. Don't change duration.py or test_meta.py
Keep the rows that are already in VALID and INVALID; add your own
VALID rows are (text, expected_seconds) and must agree with the spec
INVALID rows are strings that the spec rejects
Write test_invalid(text), parametrized over INVALID, using pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) with a pattern that matches "invalid duration"
Derive rows from the spec first. Read the bug docstrings in test_meta.py only after your first run
contract: test_duration.py defines VALID: list[tuple[str, int]], INVALID: list[str], test_valid(text, expected) and test_invalid(text), both parametrized
expectedBehavior: pytest -q shows every test_valid[...] and test_invalid[...] case passing, test_rows_are_correct and test_invalid_uses_raises_with_match passing, and all six test_tables_catch[bug_...] cases passing
edgeCases: Each unit alone, and units combined
The empty string and a whitespace-only string
Units out of order or repeated
Number without a unit, unit without a number, decimals, signs, uppercase units
hints: Conceptual: go through the spec one bullet at a time and turn each bullet into at least one row. Add a row on each side of the rule where you can: '1h30m' is valid, so try '30m1h'; ' 5m ' is valid, so try '1h 30m'. Boundaries and 'nothing' inputs ('', '   ', zero) are where bugs live.

Specific: the six bugs are about whitespace around the text, the empty string, a whitespace-only string, a total of zero, the size of an hour, and unit order/repetition. Each needs a row that only a correct implementation gets right.

Implementation: add VALID rows such as ('1h', 3600), ('0s', 0) and ('  5m ', 300), and INVALID rows such as '', '   ' and '30m1h'. Then write @pytest.mark.parametrize("text", INVALID) over a test_invalid(text) whose body is a with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="invalid duration"): block around the call. Run pytest -x -vv and read which bug survives.
evaluation: All tests pass, including all six test_tables_catch cases
Rows are derived from the spec, and each has a comment saying what it protects (a plus)
No rows copied from the bug implementations without understanding: you can say which spec rule each bug breaks
